label: made
notes: A hundred and fifty years of withdrawal - a foot of shoreline a year, then one hot decade that finished it. No catastrophe, just a sea that left while people were living beside it. It left crust to the depth of a man's arm, brine beneath that in places, and, it now appears, fresh water beneath that at the centre. The last person who had seen standing water here died eighty years ago, so the book's premise is a thing nobody alive can picture: the sea did not entirely leave.
